title: Is Lost River (2014) really a bad movie?

commenti.body:
No, you aren’t a bigot for liking Lost River. I don’t know if that was maybe a bad translation but liking a film a lot of people dislike isn’t a bad thing.

But yes, I think your opinion may change as you watch more films and your tastes evolve. Beyond the issues I have with some of the performances and plotting, I think it is a very derivative work in a very noticeable way. There’s a little Refn, a little Mario Bava, a lot of Lynch, a lot of Harmony Korine. It’s the work of a first time filmmaker who hasn’t figured out a way to disguise his influences better (which happens with a lot of directors, even some of the greats). 

And if you’ve seen and loved something like Blue Velvet, Lost River can a bit like a student film version of the classics. But if you still enjoy it, go you. You just became a cult film fan.

I enjoyed the movie as well, it has a lot going for it, especially its atmosphere and soundtrack. As you watch more movies, you'll eventually start spotting the influences that helped shape it, and it may become slightly less special or unique, but that shouldn't detract from your first experience. We all have movies we've watched early on that completely changed our perspective on cinema and what it could achieve.

First of all, thank you for your kindness. 

Yes, I get what you mean and I'll dive deeper in their work in the following weeks.

I think the "first time filmmaker" thing may have played a big part in my liking of the movie because at the time I wanted to become one myself and I think that maybe I felt like this was so huge for a first.

I totally get the "student film version" and I'll see if now it indeed throws me off, which may be did not happen at the time because I could have projected myself too hard lol. But I'm really hyped about discovering these new movies and directors (I'm taking notes of the ones you quoted) and can't wait to watch new stuff and maybe like it even more.

I'll see if Lost River will lose its shining spot but, yeah, if I still like it, I think I can't help but have a dedicated spot in my heart for it.

Thank you really much for your kind words

Thank you so much! It feels really easing to not be alone in this. Yeah I think that sooner or later, when my own references get richer, it will eventually lose some of it uniqueness but that first time watching, how it moved me, changed my view on movies and what it brought me will always be there and what came from that feeling too.

Also I'm glad to see not every film enthusiast did hate it!

Any film that gets you more into film will always have a place in your heart. And if all the reference points are new to you, it’ll probably feel fresher than someone who has seen a lot of older cinema. It’s the same reason Joker was very popular with people who haven’t delved into Martin Scorsese’s filmography. 

There are loads of films that aren’t considered classics that I love because I saw them at the right time in life. I might be the only person who has Frank (2014) as one of their favourite films.

I remember liking the movie a lot when I first watched it, especially the tone, music and visuals. I would have to rewatch it to see if it holds up for me. I definitely understand the people saying how it is very obviously "inspired" by other movies and isn't very original

Lost River isn’t really a bad movie. It just takes a lot of obvious inspiration from other works. To me, it gives those influences the homage treatment rather than ripping them off. A strong visual style, archetypal characters, and allegorical storylines are perfectly fits for young teenage audiences. It’s no wonder that it made a big impression on you!  

I think you might learn a lot going through the Letterboxd reviews for this movie. [This one](https://letterboxd.com/elihayes/film/lost-river/) in particular will give you a lot to chew on.

Yes that's so true, for me the first one was Virgin Suicides. Well I've seen a few older movies but mostly French or too unknown. Like I would watch **a lot** of movies but it took me years to watch movies like Shining for example.

Ho yeah I see the Joker / Scorsese parallel. At the time I did not like the Joker but something about it felt very entertaining.

  
Yesss, and I feel like that's so important. You're not a machine watching good or bad movies and some "dumb" movies I watched hit me just right at the time. (to get back to Lost River I felt like it was not only a right movie right time but something more for me, I found it deeply great, not just because I was a teen, which is why I made the post)

Frank was so fun! (Not in a funny happy way, don't get me wrong). Not one of my favorites but I can totally see how charming it can be. I liked it a lot.
Thank you for your answer, makes me feel less lonely. And yes, I think the references it has will appear clearer when I watch them.

Yes I totally get the homage treatment and I remember thinking at the time (not about this movie but about my future potential work) that if I had nothing to add to the table, that I wanted to show my admiration for some others' works that I found already perfect, I could still pay hommage to them without adding on to it.

This type of movie fitting the teenage audience feels so right. And the fact it was the first of this kind I watched makes it even weighs more.

I will! I only read a few on rottentomatoes and I was so shocked I made this post lol
Just read the review and it felt so good to see someone share similar opinion, will read more later! thanks!
[removed]

I had a very similar experience with Donnie Darko, of all things. I was raised on old movies, especially the ones with very black and white values. As a teen, I had seen anything like Donnie Darko in my entire life and definitely thought it was the pinnacle of film-making for a good few years, and was *shocked* to read actual reviews of it. It still holds a very special place in my heart and I’m still a bit of an apologist for it, but now that I’m older and have more life and movie experience under my belt, I can look at it more objectively.
Then we're both bigots bro, it's just a movie no worries. Everyone is entitled to their own tastes

There are lots of movies I really enjoy that would not be considered good movies. 

I enjoy going to restaurants for a 10 course chef’s tasting menu, I also enjoy going to Taco Bell every now and then.

Enjoy whatever brings you joy.

I don't think it's that bad. It just feels like a mishmash of a lot of styles that were influential to Gosling. I got it on Blu ray and gave it a rewatch and I think there's some interesting stuff in there.

I enjoyed it for what it is. Obviously the film wears its influences on its sleeve but that’s not a bad thing. Like Tarantino, Gosling isn’t shy on borrowing from other movies he likes and does just enough to make it his own. I mean everything has been done before and the real trick is going down a well trodded road and making it stand out.

This was me with Brick when I was a teen in the 2000s. With a few more years under my belt it’s obvious to me where it comes from. But at a time when I was just watching whatever was in front of me, it mesmerized me. 

I became a ride or die for JGL, still cheer when I see Lukas Haas in anything, still will watch most noir films. And while I don’t care as much about Rian Johnson as I used to, I’ll still stick up for his Star Wars movie when people shit on it. I might not have *loved* it exactly, but by the low standards set by most of the franchise it’s still one of the better ones.

I had never heard of it before but it seems really cool! That must have been an epic feeling! I love movies that you don't expect anything of and you finish them still confused about why it moved you like that
Thank you so much haha, good to read

Well Donnie Darko is still one of my favorites today but I'd love to hear if some particular movies made you change your mind. I feel like today Donnie Darko is just famous enough to be liked by people that don't dive too deep into film so it makes me feel great to see people talk about it and love it even if they don't know a lot about film, it makes me feel good and understood if that makes sense.
Thank you for your answer. I love the "everything's been done now it's up to us to twist it" approach

Yes, same here. What was weird was that for me Lost River was a chef's meal and not a fast food... but you're right, as long as at the end of the day I had a great time eating/watching, that's what matters
It's great to have a review from a recent watch, thanks!

I mean it’s been a while since I’ve seen it but I just remember thinking that the references to the housing/financial crisis were kind of just there for the sake of being there, with no real exploration of it. And also that the ending was out of left field, I wasn’t sure what it signified and how it resolved anything.

This movie holds a special place in my heart so I'm biased in favour of it.

I also discovered it at the beginning of my film journey, though I had already seen many of it's influences. 

I think it is unfait to berate movies too much from borrowing from others. Is Lost River a masterpiece? I wouldn't say, however it is the type of movie that would certainly put a director on my radar. I don't think Refn, Korine, or Argento-contemporaties are narrative masters either, and we shouldn't look at any of these through rose-tinted glasses either (as much as I love them).

What Lost River adds to the neon visuals, marginalised characters, and mysterious narrative is a distinct fairytale element that you don't see too often in American filmmaking - and this is where it stands the strongest for me.

I'm sure there's an extra 20 minutes of footage lying around somewhere that would tie the movie up neatly.

I mean, nothing I’ve watched has made me love Donnie Darko less simply because it’s so sentimental and not a *bad* movie by any metric. But a good twenty years of movie watching and life experience since then has made it feel less “deep” and extraordinary. It was so new to me at a younger age that it felt like it must contain some vital truth and grand importance. It was new to me the way that the band Belle & Sebastian seemed completely original to me - I simply didn’t have the breadth of knowledge to know a pastiche or homage when I saw one.

Yes, I remember my film teacher saying he didn't dislike the movie but he felt like the whole financial crisis critic was not pushed far enough.

I get what you felt about the ending but it did work well on me lol

First of all, always love to read someone else loves the movie the same way I do.

I totally get what you mean, I don't know a lot of their work but some of their movies I've watched are great, that's not a question but the narration can be very tame compared to other aspect of the movie (which, again, do work well) but I can sometimes feel like some aspects of the movie are a bit underwhelming and I feel like Lost River could use some of this privilege, like yes, story could be better, but it still holds well.

The fairytale element was so important for me, it made everything make sense to me, like tied everything together, even the weak points could be "saved" thanks to that fairytale "excuse", that, at the time, just felt so right.

Would have loved to see it, a crazy director's cut, of just more Lost River, can't refuse it. I totally agree, juste few scenes to explain more some of the underdeveloped concepts would have felt great.
